name: Paris
description: The French capital spreads along both banks of the Seine and has been a byword for romance and haute couture for centuries. The Eiffel Tower, the Louvre and Notre-Dame draw millions of visitors from around the world every year.
fact: The Eiffel Tower was built as a temporary structure for the 1889 world's fair and was meant to be pulled down twenty years later.

name: London
description: The British capital sits on the Thames and combines centuries of royal tradition with its role as the largest financial centre in Europe. Big Ben, Tower Bridge and the red double-decker buses are recognised the world over.
fact: The name Big Ben originally belonged only to the great bell inside the tower, not to the tower as a whole.

name: New York
description: The largest city in the United States is made up of five boroughs and mixes the skyscrapers of Manhattan with Central Park and the shores of three rivers. Wall Street, Broadway and the Statue of Liberty all stand here, symbols of the American dream.
fact: New York picked up the nickname the Big Apple back in the 1920s, from the jockeys who rode at its racetracks.

name: Tokyo
description: The Japanese capital is one of the most densely populated megacities on Earth, where skyscrapers stand next to Shinto shrines and blossoming cherry trees. Tokyo is known for its technology, its sushi and the crowded Shibuya crossing.
fact: Shibuya Crossing in Tokyo is considered one of the busiest pedestrian crossings in the world.

name: Rome
description: The Eternal City on seven hills was the heart of the Roman Empire and remains a treasury of ancient and Christian architecture. The Colosseum, the Pantheon and the Vatican make it one of the most visited cities anywhere.
fact: Legend has it that a traveller who throws a coin into the Trevi Fountain is certain to return to Rome.

name: Barcelona
description: The capital of Catalonia sits on the Mediterranean coast and is famous for the fantastical architecture of Antoni Gaudí, including the still-unfinished Sagrada Família. The city is also known for its football club and the broad promenade of La Rambla.
fact: The Sagrada Família has been under construction for more than a hundred and forty years and is still not finished.

name: Madrid
description: The Spanish capital sits in the very centre of the country and is known for the Prado museum, the Royal Palace and a nightlife that runs until dawn. Its emblem is a bear reaching up to a strawberry tree, taken from the city's coat of arms.
fact: Madrid's coat of arms, with its bear and strawberry tree, stands as a statue on the Puerta del Sol square.

name: Berlin
description: The German capital lived through its division into East and West Berlin and the fall of the Wall in 1989, which turned the city into a symbol of the country's reunification. Today it is a centre of contemporary art, street art and techno clubs.
fact: Short stretches of the Berlin Wall have been kept as a monument and painted by artists from all over the world.

name: Amsterdam
description: The Dutch capital is built on a web of canals and known for its cycling culture, its narrow houses along the water and the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum. There are more bicycles here than there are residents.
fact: Thousands of bicycles are pulled out of Amsterdam's canals every year, dropped in by accident or simply abandoned.

name: Prague
description: The Czech capital on the banks of the Vltava has kept its medieval skyline of Gothic spires and tiled roofs. Prague Castle and Charles Bridge make it one of the most atmospheric cities in Europe.
fact: The astronomical clock on Prague's Old Town Square is the oldest one in the world still in working order.

name: Vienna
description: For centuries the Austrian capital was the centre of music and of the Habsburg monarchy; Mozart, Beethoven and Strauss all lived and worked here. The city is known for its coffee houses, its opera and Schönbrunn Palace.
fact: In Vienna's coffee houses tradition lets you sit for hours over a single cup, reading the newspapers left out for guests.

name: Budapest
description: The Hungarian capital was born when Buda and Pest, on opposite banks of the Danube, merged, and it is famous for thermal baths fed by natural hot springs. The parliament building on the embankment is one of the most recognisable in Europe.
fact: The Széchenyi Baths in Budapest run on natural thermal springs and have been open for more than a century.

name: Istanbul
description: The largest city to sprawl across two continents at once is split by the Bosphorus into a European and an Asian half. Istanbul was the capital of Byzantium and then of the Ottoman Empire, as Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque still attest.
fact: Over its history Hagia Sophia has been a church, then a mosque, then a museum, and a mosque once again.

name: Dubai
description: The largest city in the UAE grew from a modest port into one of the emblems of luxury and futuristic architecture on the Persian Gulf. Here stand the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world, and the artificial islands of Palm Jumeirah.
fact: The Burj Khalifa is so tall that on its upper floors the sun sets a few minutes later than it does at the base.

name: Moscow
description: The Russian capital is the country's largest city, with centuries of history whose heart is still the Kremlin with its cathedrals and Red Square. The domes of Saint Basil's stand within sight of the towers of the Moscow City business district.
fact: The Moscow metro is famous for stations with marble, mosaics and chandeliers, conceived as underground palaces for the people.

name: Saint Petersburg
description: Founded by Peter the Great as a window on Europe, the city on the Neva became one of the world's cultural capitals thanks to the Hermitage, its drawbridges and its palace ensembles. In summer come the famous white nights.
fact: During the white nights in Saint Petersburg the sun barely sets and the city stays light until well past midnight.

name: Los Angeles
description: The largest city in California is the world capital of film and show business, thanks to the Hollywood district and its famous sign up on the hills. The beaches of Santa Monica and the big studio lots are here too.
fact: The HOLLYWOOD sign on the hills began as a property advertisement and originally read HOLLYWOODLAND.

name: San Francisco
description: The city on the Californian hills is famous for the Golden Gate Bridge, its cable cars and the former prison of Alcatraz on an island in the bay. Silicon Valley took shape just outside the city.
fact: The Golden Gate Bridge is painted orange so that it stays visible in the fog that so often covers the city.

name: Las Vegas
description: This city in the Nevada desert grew up around its casinos and became the world capital of gambling and glittering shows. The hotels of the famous Strip, each a theme park in its own right, can be seen from space at night.
fact: In Las Vegas you can get married in the middle of the night at any of the city's round-the-clock wedding chapels.

name: Chicago
description: The largest city in the American Midwest stands on the shore of Lake Michigan and is regarded as the birthplace of the modern skyscraper. Architecture cruises along the Chicago River and the Willis Tower draw anyone who loves building tall.
fact: Once a year the Chicago River is dyed bright green to mark Saint Patrick's Day.

name: Miami
description: This resort city in southern Florida is known for the beaches of Miami Beach, its pastel art deco architecture and a strong Latin American influence. It is a favourite holiday destination and one of the busiest cruise ports anywhere.
fact: The South Beach district of Miami holds one of the largest collections of art deco buildings in the world.

name: Washington, D.C.
description: The capital of the United States was laid out as a separate federal district and built up with monumental seats of power. The White House, the Capitol and the memorials on the National Mall make the city a symbol of American politics.
fact: Building heights in Washington are limited by law, so the city has almost no skyscrapers and keeps a low skyline.

name: Boston
description: One of the oldest cities in the United States played a key part in the War of Independence and is still a major centre of research, with Harvard and MIT next door. Its historic quarters and the Freedom Trail recall that revolutionary past.
fact: The Boston Tea Party of 1773, the prelude to the War of Independence, took place in the city's own harbour.

name: Seattle
description: This port city in the north-west of the United States is known for the Space Needle, its rainy weather and the fact that the Starbucks chain began here. Seattle is also the birthplace of grunge and of bands such as Nirvana.
fact: Starbucks started in Seattle in 1971, and its coffee shop at Pike Place Market is still open today.

name: New Orleans
description: With its French and Creole roots, this city in southern Louisiana is considered the birthplace of jazz and is famous for the yearly Mardi Gras carnival. The French Quarter, with its wrought-iron balconies and street music, sets the tone.
fact: Jazz took shape as a musical style in New Orleans at the turn of the 19th and 20th centuries.

name: Houston
description: The largest city in Texas grew rich on the oil industry and became home to the Johnson Space Center, from which NASA ran its missions. It is also one of the most ethnically mixed cities in the United States.
fact: The famous line "Houston, we have a problem" points to NASA's mission control centre in this very city.

name: Dallas
description: This city in northern Texas grew from a trading post into a major business hub and is known for its cowboy culture and the Dallas Cowboys football team. It is also where President John F. Kennedy was shot in 1963.
fact: The assassination of President Kennedy in Dallas in 1963 happened on the square now known as Dealey Plaza.

name: Philadelphia
description: One of the oldest cities in the United States is where the Declaration of Independence was signed, and for a time it served as the nation's capital. The cracked Liberty Bell, a symbol of American independence, is kept here.
fact: Because of its large crack, the Liberty Bell in Philadelphia has long since stopped ringing and is preserved as a relic.

name: Atlanta
description: The capital of Georgia is known as the birthplace of Martin Luther King and as one of the great transport hubs of the American South. It is also called the city of peaches, after its emblem and its many streets of that name.
fact: Atlanta's airport has ranked for years as one of the busiest airports in the world by passenger numbers.

name: Denver
description: The capital of Colorado sits exactly one mile above sea level, which earned it the nickname the Mile High City. From here the ski resorts of the Rocky Mountains are within easy reach.
fact: One step of the State Capitol in Denver carries a marker at the point exactly one mile above sea level.

name: San Diego
description: This port city in southern California, right on the Mexican border, is known for its mild climate, its beaches and one of the largest zoos in the world. It also hosts Comic-Con, the cult festival of pop culture, every year.
fact: Comic-Con, held every year in San Diego, draws more than a hundred thousand fans of comics and film.

name: Nashville
description: The capital of Tennessee is regarded as the world capital of country music and home to the legendary Grand Ole Opry. The streets downtown are lined with bars where live music plays almost around the clock.
fact: The Grand Ole Opry radio show has been broadcast from Nashville since 1925 and became the face of country music.

name: Austin
description: The capital of Texas is known as a major centre of live music and of the tech business, as well as for the yearly South by Southwest festival. The city's motto, Keep Austin Weird, sums up its creative, independent streak.
fact: The slogan Keep Austin Weird began as a show of support for local independent shops against the big chains.

name: Detroit
description: This city in Michigan is called the cradle of the American car industry: it was here that Henry Ford set up mass production of automobiles. Detroit is also known as the home of the Motown record label.
fact: It was at Ford's plants in Detroit that assembly-line car production was first used on an industrial scale.

name: Honolulu
description: The capital of Hawaii lies on the island of Oahu and is famous for Waikiki Beach and the Pearl Harbor memorial. Its gentle tropical climate makes the city one of the leading holiday destinations in the United States.
fact: The attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941 took place in a harbour just outside the centre of Honolulu.

name: Toronto
description: Canada's largest city and its financial capital is famous for the CN Tower, which for a long time was the tallest structure in the world. It is also one of the most ethnically diverse cities on the planet.
fact: The CN Tower in Toronto held the title of the world's tallest free-standing structure for more than thirty years.

name: Vancouver
description: This port city on Canada's west coast is hemmed in by mountains and ocean and is regularly named one of the most liveable cities in the world. It hosted the Winter Olympic Games in 2010.
fact: Vancouver has repeatedly topped world quality-of-life rankings, thanks to its natural setting and its mild climate.

name: Montreal
description: The largest French-speaking city in North America blends the European charm of its old quarters with a lively student scene. One of the biggest jazz festivals in the world is held here every year.
fact: The Montreal jazz festival is listed in the Guinness Book of Records as the largest jazz festival in the world.

name: Mexico City
description: The Mexican capital stands on the site of Tenochtitlan, the ancient Aztec capital, and is today one of the largest metropolises in the world. The city is known for its rich street food and its abundance of museums.
fact: Mexico City is slowly sinking, because it was built on the drained lake that once surrounded Tenochtitlan.

name: Cancún
description: This resort city on the Yucatán Peninsula grew from a fishing village into one of the main beach destinations on the Caribbean. The ruins of ancient Maya cities nearby draw anyone with an interest in history.
fact: As late as 1970 almost nobody lived where Cancún now stands: the resort was built from scratch by the Mexican government.

name: Havana
description: The Cuban capital on the Caribbean coast is famous for the colonial architecture of Old Havana, for rum and for a surviving fleet of classic American cars from the middle of the 20th century. The Malecón seafront is where the city meets.
fact: Thousands of American cars from the 1950s still drive through Havana, kept alive by decades of embargo.

name: Rio de Janeiro
description: The city at the foot of Corcovado is famous for the statue of Christ the Redeemer, the beaches of Copacabana and Ipanema and the most exuberant carnival in the world. Samba and football have long been part of who it is.
fact: The statue of Christ the Redeemer stands on Corcovado nearly seven hundred metres above the city and is visible from many districts.

name: São Paulo
description: The largest city in the southern hemisphere is Brazil's business and industrial capital, with one of the most recognisable skyscraper skylines on the continent. It is home to large Italian and Japanese communities.
fact: The Liberdade district of São Paulo is home to one of the biggest Japanese communities outside Japan.

name: Buenos Aires
description: The Argentine capital on the shore of the Río de la Plata is regarded as the birthplace of tango and is known for the European architecture of its grand central avenues. La Boca, with its brightly painted houses, is the most photographed corner of the city.
fact: Tango was born in the port districts of Buenos Aires in the late 19th century, among immigrants and dock workers.

name: Lima
description: The Peruvian capital on the Pacific coast was founded by the Spanish as the seat of colonial power in South America and has kept a rich historic core. Today Lima also counts as one of the world's great food cities.
fact: Several restaurants in Lima appear regularly on international lists of the best restaurants in the world.

name: Cusco
description: The ancient capital of the Inca empire, high in the Andes, is the starting point for journeys to Machu Picchu. Massive stonework left behind by Inca builders is still visible in the streets of the city.
fact: The Inca stone blocks in Cusco are fitted together so tightly that a knife blade will not pass between them.

name: Santiago
description: The Chilean capital lies in a valley at the foot of the Andes, whose snow-covered peaks are visible from the city centre. The region around Santiago is one of the biggest wine producers in the southern hemisphere.
fact: The ski resorts of the Andes are only a few dozen kilometres from the centre of Santiago.

name: Montevideo
description: The Uruguayan capital on the Río de la Plata is known for its long seafront promenade and for the Centenario stadium, which hosted the first football World Cup in history. Next to its giant neighbours the city stays calm and easy-going.
fact: The Centenario stadium in Montevideo was built specially for the first football World Cup in 1930.

name: Sydney
description: Australia's largest city is famous for its opera house with a roof like a set of sails and for Port Jackson harbour, spanned by one of the most recognisable bridges in the world. Bondi is among the best-known city beaches anywhere.
fact: The roof of the Sydney Opera House is covered with more than a million ceramic tiles.

name: Melbourne
description: Australia's second-largest city is known for its maze of narrow laneways full of street art and coffee shops, and for its standing as the country's sporting capital. It hosts a Formula One race and the Australian Open tennis tournament.
fact: Melbourne has been named one of the world's most liveable cities for many years running in international rankings.

name: Auckland
description: New Zealand's largest city spreads among dozens of extinct volcanic cones and two harbours on opposite sides of a narrow isthmus. The crowds of yachts in its marinas earned it the nickname the City of Sails.
fact: Auckland is called the City of Sails because it has one of the highest numbers of boats per head of population in the world.

name: Hong Kong
description: A former British colony in southern China, this is one of the leading financial centres in Asia, with one of the densest concentrations of skyscrapers in the world. Victoria Harbour and the tram up to Victoria Peak are its calling cards.
fact: Hong Kong has one of the highest numbers of skyscrapers per square kilometre of any city in the world.

name: Macau
description: This former Portuguese colony in southern China long ago overtook Las Vegas in casino revenue and is known as the Monte Carlo of Asia. Colonial Portuguese buildings and cobbled lanes survive in the historic centre.
fact: For many years now the casinos of Macau have taken in several times the revenue of the Las Vegas gambling industry.

name: Singapore
description: This city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula has turned from a modest port into one of the richest and most technologically advanced cities in the world. Its emblem is the Merlion, with a lion's head and a fish's body.
fact: The name Singapore comes from Sanskrit words meaning lion city.

name: Bangkok
description: The Thai capital combines gilded Buddhist temples and royal palaces with crowded markets and a restless nightlife. Boats still work the khlong canals, which once earned the city the name Venice of the East.
fact: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest city names in the world and is listed in the Guinness Book of Records.

name: Seoul
description: The South Korean capital grew from the ancient seat of the Joseon dynasty into one of the most technologically advanced cities in the world and the centre of K-pop. Gyeongbokgung Palace stands not far from the skyscrapers of Gangnam.
fact: The name of the Gangnam district became known around the world thanks to the song Gangnam Style.

name: Beijing
description: The Chinese capital served as the emperors' residence for many centuries, as the Forbidden City in the very heart of the metropolis still recalls. A stretch of the Great Wall of China runs not far from the city.
fact: The Forbidden City in Beijing holds almost a thousand buildings and was closed to ordinary people for centuries.

name: Shanghai
description: China's largest city, on the banks of the Huangpu, is one of the leading financial centres in the world, with the futuristic skyline of Pudong. Across the water, the Bund keeps its colonial architecture from the early 20th century.
fact: In just a few decades the former rice fields of Shanghai's Pudong district turned into a forest of skyscrapers.

name: Shenzhen
description: In only a few decades this city on the border with Hong Kong went from fishing village to one of the world's centres of electronics manufacturing. Its headlong growth became a symbol of China's economic reforms.
fact: As recently as the late 1970s the site of Shenzhen held a small fishing settlement of a few tens of thousands of people.

name: Taipei
description: The capital of Taiwan is known for night markets full of street food, for its tea culture and for Taipei 101, which held the title of the world's tallest building for several years. Green mountains press in on the dense city from every side.
fact: Inside Taipei 101 hangs a huge steel ball that damps the building's movement during typhoons and earthquakes.

name: Kyoto
description: Japan's former imperial capital has kept thousands of Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines, among them the famous red torii gates of Fushimi Inari. Its historic geisha districts give the city the atmosphere of an older Japan.
fact: Kyoto has some two thousand Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines, a number of which are on the UNESCO World Heritage list.

name: Osaka
description: Japan's third-largest city is famous for its street food, including takoyaki balls with octopus, and for the busy Dotonbori district with its blazing neon signs. Osaka Castle remains one of the city's emblems.
fact: The giant illuminated crab above a restaurant in the Dotonbori quarter has become one of Osaka's best-known sights.

name: Delhi
description: India's capital joins an ancient historic core of Mughal-era monuments, including Humayun's Tomb, to the modern government quarter of New Delhi. It is one of the most densely populated urban regions in the world.
fact: India Gate in Delhi was built as a memorial to the fallen soldiers who served in the British Indian Army.

name: Mumbai
description: India's financial capital, on the west coast of the country, is one of the most densely populated cities in the world and the home of Bollywood. The Gateway of India arch on the waterfront and the Victorian Chhatrapati Shivaji station are its emblems.
fact: India releases more feature films a year than any other country, and a sizeable share of the shooting happens in Mumbai.

name: Kathmandu
description: The Nepalese capital lies in a mountain valley at the foot of the Himalayas and serves as the starting point for climbs on Everest. The city has kept many ancient Buddhist stupas and Hindu temples that are on the UNESCO list.
fact: Almost every route taken by climbers heading for Everest begins in Kathmandu.

name: Kuala Lumpur
description: The Malaysian capital is known for the Petronas Twin Towers, for a long time the tallest buildings in the world, and for its mix of Malay, Chinese and Indian cultures. Tropical jungle surrounds the city on all sides.
fact: The Petronas Towers are joined by a skybridge at the forty-first floor, one of the highest two-storey bridges in the world.

name: Jakarta
description: The Indonesian capital, on the island of Java, is one of the largest cities in South East Asia, known for its dense scooter traffic and for how fast the ground is sinking below sea level. The government has already begun moving the capital to Borneo.
fact: Jakarta is considered one of the fastest-sinking cities in the world, which is why Indonesia is building a new capital on Borneo.

name: Manila
description: The capital of the Philippines, on Manila Bay, has kept Intramuros, the Spanish colonial quarter with its fortress walls and old churches. By density of building it is one of the most crowded cities in the world.
fact: The Intramuros district of Manila was built by the Spanish in the 16th century as a fortified town inside city walls.

name: Hanoi
description: The Vietnamese capital has kept its French colonial architecture and an old quarter of narrow trading lanes around the Lake of the Returned Sword. Street food, pho soup above all, is part of everyday life here.
fact: Legend says Hoan Kiem Lake in central Hanoi got its name after a giant turtle took back a magic sword from the emperor.

name: Ho Chi Minh City
description: Vietnam's largest city, once called Saigon, remains the country's business and trading centre, with dense rivers of motorbikes in its streets. Buildings from the French colonial era survive here, among them the Notre-Dame cathedral.
fact: The city was renamed Ho Chi Minh City in 1976 after the Vietnamese revolutionary leader, but many residents still call it Saigon.

name: Cairo
description: The Egyptian capital on the Nile is the largest city in the Arab world, and the pyramids of Giza and the Great Sphinx rise at its edge. The medieval Islamic heart of the city is on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
fact: The pyramids of Giza do not stand in open desert but right on the edge of Cairo, almost up against the built-up streets.

name: Marrakesh
description: This city at the foot of the Atlas Mountains is known for the labyrinth of souks in its medina and the crowded Jemaa el-Fnaa square with its snake charmers and street musicians. The reddish clay of its buildings gave it the name the Red City.
fact: Marrakesh is called the Red City for the terracotta shade traditionally used on the walls of the old centre.

name: Casablanca
description: Morocco's largest city and its main economic centre owes its fame to the 1942 Hollywood film of the same name, though most of the picture was shot on sound stages in the United States. The Hassan II Mosque here is one of the largest in the world.
fact: Although the film "Casablanca" made the city famous worldwide, it was shot almost entirely on studio sets in California.

name: Cape Town
description: This city in the south-west of South Africa sits at the foot of flat-topped Table Mountain on the Atlantic coast, not far from the southern tip of Africa. Offshore lies Robben Island, where Nelson Mandela spent years in prison.
fact: Nelson Mandela spent a large part of his imprisonment in the jail on Robben Island, just off Cape Town.

name: Johannesburg
description: South Africa's largest city grew up around gold mines in the late 19th century and remains the country's main business centre. The township of Soweto played a key part in the history of the struggle against apartheid.
fact: Johannesburg grew up in a matter of years after one of the world's biggest gold deposits was found in 1886.

name: Nairobi
description: The Kenyan capital is one of the few big cities in the world with a genuine national park, complete with wild lions and giraffes, right on its boundary. Nairobi is also the headquarters of several UN agencies.
fact: Nairobi National Park lies a couple of kilometres from the downtown skyscrapers, and giraffes and lions are often photographed against them.

name: Lagos
description: Nigeria's largest city and one of the fastest-growing in Africa spreads across lagoons on the Atlantic coast. It is the centre of the Nigerian film industry, Nollywood, and of a lively Afrobeats music scene.
fact: Nollywood, the Nigerian film industry largely based in Lagos, is one of the biggest in the world by the number of films released a year.

name: Jerusalem
description: One of the oldest cities in the world is held sacred by three religions at once: Judaism, Christianity and Islam. The Old City, with the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Dome of the Rock, is on the UNESCO list.
fact: The Old City of Jerusalem is traditionally divided into four quarters: Jewish, Christian, Muslim and Armenian.

name: Tel Aviv
description: This young city on Israel's Mediterranean coast is known for its beaches, its restless nightlife and one of the largest collections of Bauhaus architecture in the world. It is often called the country's technology and start-up hub.
fact: More than four thousand Bauhaus buildings, put up by architects who emigrated from Europe, earned Tel Aviv the nickname the White City.

name: Doha
description: The Qatari capital on the Persian Gulf has turned in short order from a small pearl-diving settlement into a city of futuristic skyscrapers. In 2022 Doha and the towns around it hosted the final of the football World Cup.
fact: As late as the middle of the 20th century Doha's economy rested on pearl diving, before oil and gas revenue replaced it.

name: Abu Dhabi
description: The capital of the UAE, on an island in the Persian Gulf, combines oil wealth with ambitious cultural projects, among them a branch of the Louvre. The Sheikh Zayed Mosque, with its snow-white domes, is one of the largest in the world.
fact: The Sheikh Zayed Mosque in Abu Dhabi is laid with one of the largest hand-woven carpets in the world.

name: Riyadh
description: The Saudi capital, in the middle of the Arabian Peninsula, is turning fast from a conservative administrative centre into a city of ambitious architecture. The Kingdom Centre tower, with an arch at its top, is one of its emblems.
fact: The Kingdom Centre tower in Riyadh is crowned by a viewing bridge across its arch, some three hundred metres up.

name: Tehran
description: The Iranian capital spreads out at the foot of the snow-capped Alborz mountains and remains the country's largest city and its cultural centre. Its museums hold the jewels of the Persian shahs, including the famous Peacock Throne.
fact: The vault of the Central Bank of Iran in Tehran displays one of the richest collections of jewels in the world.

name: Venice
description: This city on a lagoon of the Adriatic is built on a hundred or so small islands joined by bridges and canals instead of streets. Saint Mark's Square and a ride in a gondola remain the enduring symbols of Venice.
fact: During the seasonal acqua alta floods, Saint Mark's Square regularly goes under water and wooden walkways are laid across it.

name: Florence
description: The capital of the Italian region of Tuscany is regarded as the cradle of the Renaissance; Michelangelo, Botticelli and Leonardo da Vinci all worked here. The dome of Santa Maria del Fiore dominates every view of the city.
fact: Michelangelo's statue of David originally stood out in the open air on Florence's main square.

name: Milan
description: Italy's business capital counts as one of the world capitals of fashion and design, hosting high fashion weeks twice a year. The Duomo, with its lacework of spires, is one of the largest Gothic churches in the world.
fact: Milan's cathedral took almost six centuries of building before it was finally complete.

name: Naples
description: This port city in southern Italy, at the foot of Mount Vesuvius, is considered the birthplace of the classic margherita pizza. Nearby lie the ruins of Pompeii, destroyed by an eruption of the volcano almost two thousand years ago.
fact: The margherita pizza is said to be named after Queen Margherita of Savoy, who liked the colours of the Italian flag in it.

name: Lisbon
description: The Portuguese capital spreads over seven hills at the mouth of the Tagus and is known for the old yellow trams that wind through its narrow streets. The melancholy music of fado was born in the taverns of this city.
fact: Fado, now on the UNESCO list of intangible heritage, began in the port districts of Lisbon.

name: Porto
description: Portugal's second-largest city gave its name to port, the fortified wine aged for centuries in cellars along the Douro. Its historic centre of brightly coloured houses is on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
fact: Port wine takes its name from the city of Porto, from which it was shipped around the world for centuries.

name: Seville
description: The capital of Spanish Andalusia is regarded as the birthplace of flamenco and is famous for its vast Gothic cathedral with the Giralda bell tower, once the minaret of a mosque. Orange trees line the streets of the old centre.
fact: Seville Cathedral is the largest Gothic cathedral in the world by volume, and its Giralda tower was first built as a minaret.

name: Valencia
description: This port city on Spain's Mediterranean coast is considered the birthplace of paella and is known for the futuristic City of Arts and Sciences. Its historic centre sits alongside the modern shapes built by Santiago Calatrava.
fact: Classic paella was invented in the countryside around Valencia, as a dish of rice, vegetables and meat.

name: Nice
description: The leading resort of the French Riviera on the Côte d'Azur is known for the Promenade des Anglais and its pebble beaches. Its mild Mediterranean climate drew the European aristocracy here long ago.
fact: The Promenade des Anglais in Nice was paid for by English aristocrats who wintered on the Côte d'Azur.

name: Marseille
description: France's oldest city and its largest Mediterranean port was founded by Greek colonists more than two thousand years ago. Bouillabaisse, a fish soup, counts as the traditional dish of Marseille cooking.
fact: Marseille was founded by Greek seafarers from Phocaea about two and a half thousand years ago.

name: Lyon
description: The city where the Rhône meets the Saône is regarded as the gastronomic capital of France and the birthplace of cinema: the Lumière brothers' factory stood here and their first film was shot at its gates. The old quarters are famous for hidden passages called traboules.
fact: The Lumière brothers' first film was shot at the gates of their own factory in Lyon and shows workers leaving at the end of a shift.

name: Monaco
description: This tiny state on the Côte d'Azur is known for the Monte Carlo casino and for the yearly Formula One race run straight through the city streets. It is one of the smallest and most densely built countries in the world.
fact: The Monaco Grand Prix circuit runs along the principality's ordinary streets, past the yacht harbour and through a tunnel.

name: Brussels
description: Belgium's capital and the de facto capital of the European Union is known for waffles, chocolate and its brewing traditions, as well as for the Manneken Pis statue. The central Grand Place is reckoned one of the most beautiful squares in Europe.
fact: The Manneken Pis statue in Brussels is dressed up in costumes from time to time for the city's festivities.

name: Bruges
description: This medieval city in northern Belgium is nicknamed the Venice of the North for the network of canals that cross its historic centre. Cobbled lanes and brick facades have survived here almost untouched.
fact: The historic centre of Bruges is so well preserved that it is on the UNESCO World Heritage list in its entirety.

name: Munich
description: The capital of Bavaria is known around the world for the Oktoberfest beer festival and for the Bayern Munich football club. Marienplatz, with its town hall and its chiming clock, is the heart of the old city.
fact: Oktoberfest in Munich draws millions of visitors every year and, despite its name, begins back in September.

name: Hamburg
description: Germany's biggest port city, on the Elbe, is known for the Reeperbahn red-light district, where The Beatles played early in their career. The Elbphilharmonie concert hall, with its wave-like roof, has become the city's new emblem.
fact: The Beatles played an important part of their early gigs in the clubs of Hamburg's Reeperbahn district.

name: Frankfurt
description: Germany's financial capital and the seat of the European Central Bank stands out among German cities for an unusually dense cluster of skyscrapers, which earned it the name Mainhattan. The writer Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was born here.
fact: Frankfurt's high-rise skyline is so untypical of Germany that the city was nicknamed Mainhattan, after Manhattan.

name: Cologne
description: One of the oldest cities in Germany is famous for its enormous Gothic cathedral, whose spires were for a few years after completion the tallest in the world. The city is also the home of eau de cologne, the scent that took its name from it.
fact: Cologne Cathedral was built in fits and starts over more than six hundred years and was only finished in the 19th century.

name: Zurich
description: Switzerland's largest city, on the lake of the same name, is one of the leading financial centres in the world and a fixture at the top of quality-of-life rankings. The old Niederdorf quarter has kept its narrow medieval lanes.
fact: Zurich regularly ranks at the top of international lists of cities with the highest quality of life.

name: Geneva
description: The city on the shore of Lake Geneva is the European headquarters of the UN and home to a crowd of international organisations. The Jet d'Eau fountain, shooting straight out of the lake, can be seen from almost anywhere in town.
fact: The plume of the Jet d'Eau in Geneva rises more than a hundred metres and is visible for many kilometres around.

name: Salzburg
description: The birthplace of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart has kept its baroque historic centre below the old Hohensalzburg fortress. A large part of the film "The Sound of Music" was shot here as well.
fact: The house where Mozart was born, in the centre of Salzburg, is now a museum and one of the city's chief attractions.

name: Copenhagen
description: The Danish capital, on the island of Zealand, is known for the coloured houses along the Nyhavn waterfront, its cycling culture and the Little Mermaid statue by the water. The city is regularly named one of the most liveable in the world.
fact: The Little Mermaid statue in Copenhagen was put up in honour of Hans Christian Andersen's tale and became the city's emblem.

name: Stockholm
description: The Swedish capital spreads across some fifteen islands joined by bridges, between Lake Mälaren and the Baltic Sea. The old town of Gamla Stan has kept its medieval plan of narrow lanes.
fact: Stockholm is often called the Venice of the North, because it is built on more than a dozen islands.

name: Oslo
description: The Norwegian capital sits at the head of the scenic Oslofjord, ringed by wooded hills where you can ski straight out from the city centre. The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded here every year.
fact: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo every year, while the other Nobel prizes are handed out in Stockholm.

name: Helsinki
description: The Finnish capital on the Baltic is known for the severe neoclassical architecture of Senate Square and for an enormous number of saunas per head of population. The city is a regular at the top of quality-of-life rankings.
fact: Saunas in Helsinki turn up in ordinary blocks of flats and in offices, and the public city saunas are again fashionable places to meet.

name: Reykjavík
description: The northernmost capital in the world is the starting point for trips to Iceland's geysers, glaciers and volcanoes. Thanks to geothermal energy, most of the city is heated by the natural warmth of the earth.
fact: Almost every house in Reykjavík is heated with geothermal water that comes straight out of the ground.

name: Dublin
description: The Irish capital on the river Liffey is the home of Guinness and of the writers James Joyce and Oscar Wilde. The busy Temple Bar quarter is known for its pubs with live Irish music.
fact: The Guinness brewery in Dublin signed a lease on its land in the 18th century for a term of nine thousand years.

name: Edinburgh
description: The Scottish capital grew up around an ancient castle on top of an extinct volcano and hosts the Fringe, the largest arts festival in the world, every year. The medieval Royal Mile links the castle to Holyrood Palace.
fact: The Edinburgh Fringe is reckoned the largest arts festival in the world by the number of shows and performances.

name: Manchester
description: This city in the north of England became the cradle of the industrial revolution on the back of its textile mills, and today it is known as the home of Manchester United and Manchester City. The Madchester music scene of the late 1980s started here too.
fact: Manchester is regarded as the place where the industrial revolution began in the 18th and 19th centuries, thanks to its textile mills.

name: Liverpool
description: This port city in the north-west of England is famous above all as the home of The Beatles, whose road to fame began at the local Cavern Club. The brick warehouses of the Albert Dock now hold museums and restaurants.
fact: The Cavern Club in Liverpool, where The Beatles began, was rebuilt after demolition and still works close to the original spot.

name: Athens
description: The Greek capital is considered one of the cradles of European civilisation, of philosophy and of democracy. Above the city rises the Acropolis with the Parthenon, built back in the 5th century BC.
fact: The owl was the sacred bird of the goddess Athena and remains the unofficial symbol of the city.

name: Dubrovnik
description: This fortress city on the Adriatic coast is ringed by massive medieval walls you can walk all the way around the old town on. Its picturesque lanes made Dubrovnik one of the main filming locations for "Game of Thrones".
fact: Many of the King's Landing scenes in "Game of Thrones" were shot in the streets of old Dubrovnik.

name: Split
description: Croatia's second-largest city grew up inside and around the ancient Roman palace of the emperor Diocletian, built in the early 4th century. Cafés, shops and flats now fill the former palace walls.
fact: The historic centre of Split is in effect the surviving palace of the Roman emperor Diocletian, and people still live in it.

name: Zagreb
description: The Croatian capital divides into the Upper Town, with Gothic churches and cobbled squares, and the more modern Lower Town of museums and parks. Zagreb's Christmas markets have repeatedly been voted the best in Europe.
fact: Zagreb's Christmas market was voted the best in Europe several years in a row by visitors in an online poll.

name: Ljubljana
description: The Slovenian capital is known for the green embankments of the Ljubljanica and the castle on the hill above town, and the dragon has long been its symbol. A compact, walkable centre makes it one of the friendliest cities in Europe.
fact: The dragon has been a symbol of Ljubljana since legendary times and appears on the city's coat of arms and its bridges.

name: Bratislava
description: The Slovak capital, on the Danube, is only an hour from Vienna and has kept a compact historic centre with a castle above the river. The borders of Austria and Hungary run practically at the city limits.
fact: Bratislava is the only capital in the world that borders two other sovereign states at once.

name: Belgrade
description: The Serbian capital stands where the Danube meets the Sava and has been destroyed and rebuilt dozens of times over its history. The Kalemegdan fortress on the hill above the rivers is its emblem and its oldest part.
fact: The Kalemegdan fortress in Belgrade was rebuilt by empire after empire, from the Romans to the Ottomans and the Austrians.

name: Sofia
description: The Bulgarian capital lies at the foot of Mount Vitosha and counts as one of the oldest capitals in Europe, with a history going back thousands of years. The golden domes of the Alexander Nevsky cathedral are its chief emblem.
fact: In the centre of Sofia, within a few steps, you can see monuments from several eras at once: Roman, Ottoman and socialist.

name: Bucharest
description: Between the wars the Romanian capital was called Little Paris for the elegant architecture of its boulevards. It is also home to the Palace of the Parliament, one of the largest and heaviest administrative buildings in the world.
fact: The Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest is considered one of the heaviest buildings in the world, and only a handful exceed it in volume.

name: Warsaw
description: The Polish capital was almost completely destroyed in the Second World War and then painstakingly rebuilt from old drawings and paintings. The mermaid on its coat of arms is taken as the symbol of the city.
fact: The historic centre of Warsaw was rebuilt after the war so faithfully that it was put on the UNESCO World Heritage list all the same.

name: Kraków
description: Poland's former capital has kept one of the most beautiful medieval centres in Europe, with the royal castle of Wawel on the hill above the Vistula. Legend has it that a fire-breathing dragon once lived beneath the castle.
fact: At the foot of Wawel Hill in Kraków stands a dragon statue that really does breathe fire for the tourists.

name: Riga
description: The Latvian capital on the Baltic holds one of the largest collections of art nouveau architecture in Europe. Local legend has it that the first decorated Christmas tree in history stood on Riga's town hall square.
fact: Riga claims to be the city where the very first decorated Christmas tree was put up on a public square.

name: Tallinn
description: The Estonian capital, on the Gulf of Finland, has kept one of the most complete medieval old towns in Europe, with its towers and defensive walls. Today Tallinn is also known as one of the world's most advanced digital cities.
fact: The technology behind Skype was developed in Tallinn, sealing Estonia's reputation as a digital pioneer.

name: Vilnius
description: The Lithuanian capital holds one of the largest baroque old towns in Eastern Europe, with dozens of churches from different periods. The bohemian Užupis quarter has jokingly declared itself an independent republic with its own constitution.
fact: The Užupis district of Vilnius jokingly declared itself a separate republic and even adopted a tongue-in-cheek constitution.

name: Minsk
description: The Belarusian capital was almost entirely destroyed in the Second World War and rebuilt in the neoclassical style of the Stalin years. The broad Independence Avenue became the main axis of a spacious, green city.
fact: Minsk was rebuilt after the war almost from nothing, so the city centre reads as a single ensemble of Stalinist architecture.

name: Kyiv
description: The Ukrainian capital on the banks of the Dnipro is one of the oldest East Slavic cities, with a history going back to Kyivan Rus. The golden domes of the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra and Saint Sophia's are visible from the high riverside bluffs.
fact: The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra is known for its system of catacombs, where hermit monks made their cells for centuries.

name: Odesa
description: This port city on the Black Sea is famous for the Potemkin Stairs running from the harbour up to the centre, and for the dry wit of its residents. Odesa has long been known for its many-cultured character and its seaside spirit.
fact: The Potemkin Stairs in Odesa are built so that from below you see only steps and from above only landings, because the flights differ in width.

name: Tbilisi
description: The Georgian capital spreads along the narrow valley of the Kura and is known for the sulphur baths of the old Abanotubani district, which gave the city its name. A cable car links the historic centre to the Narikala fortress on the hill.
fact: The name Tbilisi comes from the Georgian word for warm, after the sulphur springs that rise here.

name: Batumi
description: This seaside resort on the Black Sea mixes subtropical greenery with bold modern architecture along the promenade. The Batumi botanical garden is one of the largest and oldest in the Caucasus.
fact: On the Batumi promenade stands a moving metal sculpture of two lovers, whose figures drift together and apart again.

name: Yerevan
description: The Armenian capital is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, older than Rome itself. From the centre of town you look out at biblical Mount Ararat, although the mountain itself now lies in neighbouring Turkey.
fact: Mount Ararat, the great symbol of Armenia, is clearly visible from Yerevan, although it formally lies outside the country.

name: Baku
description: The Azerbaijani capital on the Caspian sets the medieval Icherisheher old town against the futuristic Flame Towers, shaped like tongues of fire. The region has long been known for natural gas seeps that burned straight out of the ground.
fact: The name Azerbaijan is often linked to a Persian phrase meaning land of fire, after the burning gas seeps around Baku.

name: Almaty
description: The former capital of Kazakhstan lies at the foot of the snowy Trans-Ili Alatau and is thought to be one of the places where the domestic apple originated. It remains the country's cultural and financial centre even after the capital moved to Astana.
fact: The name Almaty comes from alma, the word for apple, and the country around the city is held to be a homeland of the cultivated apple.

name: Astana
description: The capital of Kazakhstan was built almost entirely anew on the steppe in the late 1990s and 2000s, to designs by well-known international architects. The Baiterek monument, with a sphere at its top, became the emblem of the new capital.
fact: The city has changed its name several times: from Akmola to Astana, then Nur-Sultan, and back to Astana.

name: Tashkent
description: The Uzbek capital is the largest city in Central Asia, rebuilt in a Soviet modernist style after the devastating earthquake of 1966. One of the region's oldest metro lines runs through palace-like stations decorated with national ornament.
fact: After the 1966 earthquake, builders came from all over the Soviet Union to rebuild Tashkent, and that shaped the look of the city.

name: Samarkand
description: One of the oldest cities in Central Asia was the capital of Tamerlane's empire and a key stop on the Silk Road. The turquoise domes and mosaics of the Registan square count as the summit of Central Asian architecture.
fact: The Registan in Samarkand is framed by three madrasas built in different centuries that still form a single architectural ensemble.

name: Bukhara
description: This ancient city on the Silk Road has kept one of the most complete Islamic historic centres in Central Asia, with its minarets, madrasas and domes. The Kalyan minaret served for centuries as a landmark for caravans crossing the desert.
fact: Legend says the Kalyan minaret in Bukhara so impressed Genghis Khan that he ordered it spared when the city fell.

name: Antalya
description: This resort city on Turkey's Mediterranean coast is one of the country's main tourist centres, with sandy beaches and the old harbour quarter of Kaleiçi. Ancient Greek and Roman ruins survive not far from the city.
fact: Hadrian's Gate in the old town of Antalya was built for the visit of the Roman emperor Hadrian almost two thousand years ago.

name: Kazan
description: The capital of Tatarstan, where the Kazanka meets the Volga, sets Orthodox cathedrals beside the minarets of the Kul Sharif mosque inside its ancient kremlin. The legendary winged serpent Zilant is taken as the symbol of the city.
fact: The Kul Sharif mosque and the Orthodox Annunciation Cathedral stand side by side within the same Kazan kremlin.

name: Sochi
description: This resort city on Russia's Black Sea coast combines subtropical beaches with the ski slopes of Krasnaya Polyana a short way inland. Sochi hosted the Winter Olympic Games in 2014.
fact: Sochi was the warmest city ever to host a Winter Olympics: the events ran in the subtropics right beside the sea.

name: Yekaterinburg
description: This big industrial city in the Urals stands almost on the notional border between Europe and Asia, marked by an obelisk nearby. It was founded as a mining and metalworking centre and long mattered for quarrying and cutting stone.
fact: An obelisk near Yekaterinburg marks the notional boundary between Europe and Asia.

name: Novosibirsk
description: The largest city in Siberia grew out of a settlement built around a bridge over the Ob for the Trans-Siberian Railway in the late 19th century. Today it is the region's main centre of science and business, with a large academic town.
fact: Novosibirsk owes its founding to the construction of a railway bridge over the Ob for the Trans-Siberian line.

name: Nizhny Novgorod
description: The city where the Oka joins the Volga was for centuries Russia's most important trading centre, thanks to the largest fair in the country. Its kremlin on the high bank is reckoned one of the mightiest in Russia.
fact: In the 19th century the Nizhny Novgorod fair was one of the largest in the world and largely set trading prices across Russia.

name: Kaliningrad
description: Russia's westernmost large city, formerly known by its German name of Königsberg, was handed to the USSR after the Second World War. The region around it is the world's biggest source of amber.
fact: The coast of the Kaliningrad region holds the largest proven reserves of amber in the world.

name: Vladivostok
description: Russia's main Pacific port is the eastern terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railway, which runs the whole length of the country. The cable-stayed bridge across the Eastern Bosphorus strait is one of the modern city's emblems.
fact: Vladivostok is closer to Tokyo and Seoul than to Moscow, almost nine thousand kilometres away along the Trans-Siberian.

name: Irkutsk
description: This old Siberian city on the Angara is the main gateway to Lake Baikal, the largest freshwater lake on the planet by volume. In the 19th century it became a place of exile for the Decembrists, which left a clear mark on its culture.
fact: Irkutsk is often called the gateway to Baikal, the world's largest store of fresh water by volume.

name: Perth
description: The capital of Western Australia is considered one of the most isolated big cities in the world: the nearest other metropolis is thousands of kilometres away. The black swan, first described by Europeans here, became the emblem of city and state.
fact: Perth is often named one of the cities furthest from any other large city in the world.

name: Brisbane
description: The capital of Queensland, on the Brisbane River, is known for its warm subtropical climate and for being the gateway to the beaches of the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast. The city is preparing to host the 2032 Summer Olympics.
fact: Brisbane will host the 2032 Summer Olympics, the third Olympic Games in Australian history.

name: Phoenix
description: The capital of Arizona lies in the Sonoran Desert and counts as one of the sunniest and hottest big cities in the United States. It has grown fast in recent decades on the strength of its comfortable winters, drawing people from all over the country.
fact: In summer the thermometer in Phoenix regularly passes forty degrees; the city has some of the hottest average temperatures in the country.

name: San Antonio
description: This city in southern Texas grew up around the Spanish mission of the Alamo, where the famous siege of 1836 took place during the Texas war of independence. Today San Antonio is known for the winding River Walk, lined with cafés and boat rides right downtown.
fact: The Alamo, now the emblem of the city, was originally built as a Catholic mission long before the famous siege.

name: San Jose
description: This city at the southern end of San Francisco Bay is the unofficial capital of Silicon Valley: the headquarters of a great many technology companies sit here and nearby. For all that, San Jose stays quieter and more spread out than San Francisco.
fact: San Jose was California's first capital after the territory joined the United States, though it held the title only briefly.

name: Jacksonville
description: This city in north-eastern Florida spreads along both banks of the St Johns River and covers more land inside its limits than almost any other city in the country. Jacksonville is a big port and industrial centre, with long Atlantic beaches nearby.
fact: By land area Jacksonville is one of the largest cities in the United States, largely because city and county merged in 1968.

name: Columbus
description: The capital of Ohio stands on the Scioto River and remains one of the fastest-growing cities in the American Midwest. Ohio State University, and its football team, shape much of life in the city.
fact: Columbus is named after Christopher Columbus and was founded specially to be the new capital of Ohio.

name: Charlotte
description: North Carolina's largest city became the second most important banking centre in the United States after New York, thanks to the headquarters of major financial corporations. Its name honours Queen Charlotte, consort of the British king George III.
fact: Charlotte's business district is called not downtown, as in most American cities, but Uptown.

name: Indianapolis
description: The capital of Indiana was laid out almost at the centre of the state, on a regular plan reminiscent of Washington. It made its name with the Indy 500, one of the oldest and most prestigious motor races in the world, run here since the early 20th century.
fact: The Indianapolis Motor Speedway, home of the Indy 500, has one of the largest permanent spectator capacities of any sports venue in the world.

name: Fort Worth
description: This city in northern Texas grew out of an army fort and a cattle staging post, and it still takes pride in its cowboy heritage. In the historic Stockyards district a real herd of longhorns is driven down the street twice a day.
fact: Fort Worth is called the place where the West begins, in contrast to neighbouring Dallas and its business polish.

name: El Paso
description: At the westernmost tip of Texas, this city sits on the Mexican border, directly opposite Ciudad Juárez. Together the two form one of the largest cross-border conurbations in the world, and the Franklin Mountains rise above El Paso.
fact: El Paso is regarded as one of the safest large cities in the United States, despite sitting next to troubled Ciudad Juárez.

name: Memphis
description: This city on the Mississippi is considered the cradle of blues and rock and roll: the sound of American popular music took shape on Beale Street. Memphis is also home to Graceland, Elvis Presley's estate and a place of pilgrimage for his fans.
fact: Elvis Presley's Graceland mansion in Memphis is one of the most visited private homes in the United States, open to visitors since 1982.

name: Louisville
description: Kentucky's largest city stands on the Ohio River and hosts the Kentucky Derby every year, one of the most prestigious horse races in America. Louisville is also known as the home of the Louisville Slugger baseball bat.
fact: The Derby has been run since 1875, and the winner is draped in a blanket of red roses, hence the nickname the Run for the Roses.

name: Milwaukee
description: This city on the western shore of Lake Michigan is known for its German heritage and its brewing traditions: several of the biggest American beer companies were headquartered here. Milwaukee is also famous for an art museum with wings that open like sails.
fact: Every summer Milwaukee's lakefront hosts Summerfest, one of the largest music festivals in the world.

name: Portland
description: This city in the north-west of the United States is known for its care about the environment, its dense network of bike lanes and its many craft breweries and coffee shops. Portland sits where the Willamette meets the Columbia, with Mount Hood rising nearby.
fact: Portland is home to Powell's, one of the largest bookshops in the world, where new books sit on the shelf beside second-hand ones.

name: Oklahoma City
description: The capital of Oklahoma grew up on a site settled almost overnight during the famous land run of 1889. The city has close ties to the oil industry: derricks once stood even on the grounds of the state capitol.
fact: The well beside the state capitol was drilled straight through a flower bed, which is why it was nicknamed Petunia Number One.

name: Albuquerque
description: New Mexico's largest city lies in the valley of the Rio Grande, about a mile and a half above sea level. Every year it hosts the largest balloon festival in the world, filling the sky above the city with hundreds of colours.
fact: The legendary Route 66 ran through the city, and its trace survives as the long Central Avenue.

name: Tucson
description: This city in southern Arizona is ringed by mountains and by the Sonoran Desert with its signature saguaro cacti, which gave the neighbouring national park its name. Tucson is known for its observatories, drawn here by the dry air and clear night skies.
fact: Because its skies are so dark, Tucson limits street lighting so as not to disturb the observatories nearby.

name: Sacramento
description: The capital of California stands where the American River joins the Sacramento and owes its growth to the gold rush of the mid-19th century. Today the city is known for the dome of the state capitol and as the hub of the farming country of the Sacramento Valley.
fact: Because the rivers kept flooding, the streets of old Sacramento were raised several metres in the 19th century, houses and all.

name: Kansas City
description: This city on the Missouri-Kansas line is an important centre of jazz, with a rich musical heritage from the early 20th century, and the home of its own style of barbecue. It has more fountains than almost any other city, hence the name City of Fountains.
fact: The city sits right on the state line: there is another Kansas City next door, on the Kansas side.

name: Omaha
description: Nebraska's largest city stands on the Missouri River and is known as the home of the investor Warren Buffett and his holding company Berkshire Hathaway. Historically Omaha was an important point in the cattle and meatpacking industry of the American Midwest.
fact: The annual Berkshire Hathaway shareholders' meeting in Omaha draws tens of thousands of investors from around the world.

name: Raleigh
description: The capital of North Carolina forms part of the Research Triangle with Durham and Chapel Hill, a cluster of major universities and technology companies. Raleigh is called the City of Oaks for its many green parks and the old trees along its streets.
fact: Raleigh is named after the English adventurer Sir Walter Raleigh, who never set foot in North America himself.

name: Colorado Springs
description: This city at the foot of Pikes Peak in the Rocky Mountains is known for its military installations, including the US Air Force Academy and the NORAD command centre inside nearby Cheyenne Mountain. Clean mountain air and the views made it a popular resort.
fact: A cog railway climbs to the summit of Pikes Peak, and the view from up there inspired the words of "America the Beautiful".

name: Virginia Beach
description: This seaside city in south-eastern Virginia boasts one of the longest beaches on the east coast of the United States and a long oceanfront boardwalk. Besides tourism, it is closely tied to major naval and air force bases.
fact: Norfolk sits next door, home to the largest naval base in the world.

name: Baltimore
description: This port city on Chesapeake Bay is known for the renewed historic Inner Harbor and for blocks of narrow brick row houses. Edgar Allan Poe lived and died here, and his grave in the city centre is still a place of pilgrimage for readers.
fact: The words of the American national anthem were written here, sketched out by a witness to the defence of Fort McHenry in 1814.

name: Minneapolis
description: This city on the banks of the Mississippi is called the City of Lakes: more than a dozen lie within its limits, and park trails lead to almost every one. With neighbouring Saint Paul it forms the conurbation known as the Twin Cities.
fact: Minneapolis grew up as a centre of flour milling, on the power of the Saint Anthony Falls on the Mississippi.

name: Tampa
description: This city on Florida's west coast stands on Tampa Bay and counts as one of the stormiest places in the United States, which earned it the name lightning capital of the country. The cigar trade once made it the cigar capital of the world.
fact: The Ybor City district of Tampa was once called the cigar capital of the world, for its dozens of hand-rolling factories.

name: Orlando
description: This city in central Florida became the world capital of theme parks after Walt Disney World opened in 1971, with Universal Studios and others following. Tourism has turned Orlando into one of the most visited cities in the United States.
fact: The Walt Disney World site outside Orlando is comparable in area to a small town and holds several separate parks.

name: St. Louis
description: The city where the Missouri meets the Mississippi is called the Gateway to the West: for centuries settlers set out from here into the American frontier. Its symbol is the giant steel Gateway Arch, the tallest monument in the United States.
fact: Inside the arch runs an unusual tram of capsules that carries visitors up to the viewing deck at the top.

name: Pittsburgh
description: The city where three rivers meet was once the world capital of steel, and today it is known as the city of bridges: it has more of them than any other city in the United States. After the collapse of steel it turned to technology and medicine.
fact: The Allegheny and the Monongahela come together in Pittsburgh to form the Ohio, which is where all those bridges come from.

name: Cincinnati
description: This city on the Ohio River is famous for its own style of chili, a spiced meat sauce served over spaghetti rather than on its own. Hilly ground and the old buildings of its German quarters recall the waves of European settlers in the 19th century.
fact: Cincinnati chili is traditionally served on spaghetti and ordered by the number of toppings, from two ways up to five.

name: Cleveland
description: This city on the shore of Lake Erie is known for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, devoted to the history of popular music. Cleveland sits at the mouth of the Cuyahoga, so polluted that it caught fire in 1969 and pushed the country towards environmental law.
fact: The Hall of Fame was built here because the Cleveland DJ Alan Freed did so much to popularise the very phrase rock and roll.

name: Salt Lake City
description: The capital of Utah was founded by Mormon settlers in the mid-19th century beside the Great Salt Lake, which gave the city its name. It is ringed by the Wasatch Mountains and remains the spiritual centre of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
fact: The Great Salt Lake next to the city is so salty that it is almost impossible to drown in it: the body floats by itself.

name: Anchorage
description: Alaska's largest city lies between the mountains and Cook Inlet and is home to about 40% of the state's population, despite Alaska's vast empty spaces. Moose and bears wander into its residential streets often enough.
fact: Every March the famous Iditarod dog-sled race is started ceremonially in the centre of Anchorage.

name: Buffalo
description: This city on the eastern shore of Lake Erie, near Niagara Falls, gave the world the spicy chicken wings named after it. Once an important port and industrial centre, Buffalo is also known for snowy winters fed by lake-effect storms.
fact: Buffalo wings were first made in Buffalo itself, at the Anchor Bar, in the early 1960s.

name: Tulsa
description: In the early 20th century this city on the Arkansas River was called the oil capital of the world, thanks to the drilling boom in the region. Its historic Greenwood district was once one of the most successful Black business quarters in the country, known as Black Wall Street.
fact: In 1921 Greenwood was destroyed in the Tulsa race massacre, events that went almost unspoken of in America for decades.

name: Fresno
description: This city in the heart of California's Central Valley is one of the state's main farming centres, with endless vineyards, orchards and cotton fields around it. Fresno is often called the raisin capital of the world for the sheer volume it produces.
fact: Fresno County has long been one of the most productive farming regions in the United States by the value of its harvest.

name: Wichita
description: Kansas's largest city is called the air capital of the world: several major aircraft and aero-engine manufacturers have plants here. The city grew out of a staging post on the cattle trails of the 19th-century Wild West.
fact: The first Pizza Hut opened in Wichita in 1958, started by two local student brothers.

name: Santa Fe
description: The capital of New Mexico is one of the oldest cities founded by Europeans in what is now the United States, known for its earthen adobe architecture. Santa Fe has long counted as a notable centre of art, with a great many galleries and museums.
fact: Santa Fe is the highest state capital in the United States, standing more than two thousand metres above sea level.

name: Savannah
description: One of the first cities in Georgia has kept its regular grid of historic squares, planted with oaks trailing Spanish moss. This port city on the Savannah River is known for its southern character and one of the largest historic districts in the country.
fact: Savannah was founded in 1733 by James Oglethorpe, who laid it out at once on a regular grid of streets and squares.

name: Charleston
description: This port city on the South Carolina coast has kept its handsome historic mansions and its cobbled colonial-era streets. It was here, in 1861, that the first shots of the American Civil War were fired at Fort Sumter in the local harbour.
fact: For its abundance of churches of every denomination, Charleston earned the nickname the Holy City.

name: Aspen
description: This small ski town in the Colorado Rockies counts as one of the most prestigious and expensive resorts in the United States, drawing celebrities from all over the world. Its name comes from the aspen groves that grow thickly in the mountains around.
fact: Despite its modest permanent population, Aspen takes in hundreds of thousands of visitors a year for its ski slopes and festivals.

name: Chelyabinsk
description: This large industrial centre in the southern Urals grew up around metalworks and engineering plants and was long closed to foreigners. In 2013 a large meteor exploded above Chelyabinsk, caught on video by hundreds of dashboard cameras.
fact: The Chelyabinsk meteor of 2013 was one of the largest recorded explosions of a body from space above an inhabited place in the last century.

name: Omsk
description: This city in western Siberia stands where the Om joins the Irtysh, and it takes its name from the smaller river. Founded as a fortress in the early 18th century, Omsk served in 1918 and 1919 as the capital of the White movement under Admiral Kolchak.
fact: Fyodor Dostoevsky spent several years in Omsk, serving the sentence of hard labour he later described in "The House of the Dead".

name: Samara
description: This city on the Volga below the Zhiguli hills was long a closed centre of the Soviet rocket and space industry, under the name Kuibyshev. Samara is known for one of the longest riverside promenades on the Volga and for a stadium built for the 2018 World Cup.
fact: The Soyuz rockets that carry cosmonauts into orbit were built in Samara for decades.

name: Rostov-on-Don
description: This city in southern Russia stands on the Don and has long been the way through to the Caucasus, which is why it is called the gateway to the Caucasus. Rostov is a major trading, industrial and cultural centre of the south, with a rich merchant past.
fact: Not far from the city, at the mouth of the Don, lie the excavations of Tanais, an ancient Greek town on the edge of the classical world.

name: Ufa
description: The capital of Bashkortostan stands where the Ufa joins the Belaya and is known for its equestrian monument to the national hero Salavat Yulaev, one of the largest in Russia. The city mixes Bashkir tradition with a developed petrochemical industry.
fact: The painter Mikhail Nesterov was born in Ufa, and the Bashkir art museum carries his name.

name: Krasnoyarsk
description: This large Siberian city on the Yenisei is known for the Stolby nature reserve, with strange rock pillars that draw climbers. Krasnoyarsk is also known for one of the hydroelectric stations on the Yenisei, whose dam became a symbol of the region.
fact: Krasnoyarsk appears on the ten-rouble note, which shows the dam of its hydro station and the chapel of Saint Paraskeva.

name: Perm
description: This city on the Kama, at the western slopes of the Urals, was for centuries the gateway to Siberia and remains a big centre of engineering and chemicals. Perm gave its name to the Permian period in geology, named after the region by the British scientist Roderick Murchison.
fact: Perm is thought to be the model for the town of Yuriatin in Boris Pasternak's novel "Doctor Zhivago".

name: Voronezh
description: This city in Russia's black-earth belt is regarded as the cradle of the Russian navy: it was here, on Peter the Great's orders, that the first Russian warships were built around the turn of the 18th century. Voronezh remains a big industrial and university centre.
fact: The Voronezh yards built the Goto Predestinatsia, the first Russian ship of the line; a replica of it stands on the waterfront today.

name: Volgograd
description: This city on the Volga, once called Stalingrad, was the site of one of the bloodiest battles of the Second World War, the one that turned the course of the whole conflict. The monument The Motherland Calls, one of the tallest statues in the world, rises above it.
fact: Volgograd stretches more than sixty kilometres along the Volga and remains one of the longest cities in Russia.

name: Krasnodar
description: The main city of the Kuban and the centre of a fertile southern region has been one of the fastest-growing cities in Russia in recent decades. Krasnodar is known for its football club and for the park of the same name, built with the money of a local businessman.
fact: Until 1920 the city was called Yekaterinodar, after Catherine the Great, who granted these lands to the Cossacks.

name: Tyumen
description: The oldest Russian city in Siberia became the administrative and financial centre of a rich oil and gas region, although the drilling itself happens further north. Tyumen is known for its many hot springs and the thermal resorts around it.
fact: Tyumen is called the gateway to Siberia: the main road east ran through it, and later so did the Trans-Siberian Railway.

name: Izhevsk
description: The capital of Udmurtia grew up around arms factories and metalworks and is known as the home of the Kalashnikov rifle. Mikhail Kalashnikov lived and worked in Izhevsk for decades, and a monument to him stands in the city centre.
fact: The Izhevsk arms works was founded in the early 19th century, and the city grew up around its mill dam on the river Izh.

name: Barnaul
description: The capital of the Altai region was founded in the 18th century as a works settlement around the Demidov family's silver smelting. Today Barnaul remains a large industrial and agricultural centre in the south of western Siberia.
fact: In Barnaul in the 1760s Ivan Polzunov built one of the world's first steam engines for use in a factory.

name: Ulyanovsk
description: This city on the Volga, once called Simbirsk, is known above all as the birthplace of Vladimir Lenin, after whom it was renamed in Soviet times. Today Ulyanovsk remains a large centre of aircraft and car manufacturing.
fact: The Presidential Bridge across the Volga at Ulyanovsk is one of the longest in Russia, at almost six kilometres.

name: Khabarovsk
description: One of the largest cities in the Russian Far East stands on the high bank of the Amur, almost on the Chinese border. Khabarovsk is the gateway to the far-eastern taiga, where the rare Amur tiger, the symbol of the region, still lives.
fact: Khabarovsk appears on the five-thousand-rouble note, which shows the monument to Muravyov-Amursky and the bridge over the Amur.

name: Yaroslavl
description: One of the oldest cities on the Volga was founded, so the story goes, by Prince Yaroslav the Wise, who killed a she-bear on this spot. Its historic centre, with an ensemble of churches and trading arcades, is on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
fact: Yaroslavl appears on the Russian thousand-rouble note, together with the monument to Yaroslav the Wise.

name: Tolyatti
description: This city on the Volga grew up around AvtoVAZ, the largest car plant in the country, which builds the Lada. Its earlier name, Stavropol, was changed in honour of the Italian communist Palmiro Togliatti.
fact: Old Stavropol-on-Volga fell inside the flood zone of the Kuibyshev reservoir, and the city had to be moved to a new site.

name: Vladimir
description: This ancient city on the Klyazma was once the capital of the powerful principality of Vladimir-Suzdal and one of the places where Russian statehood took shape. Its white-stone Assumption and Saint Demetrius cathedrals are on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
fact: The Golden Gate of Vladimir, built in the 12th century, is one of the few surviving fortifications of pre-Mongol Rus.

name: Murmansk
description: The largest city in the world above the Arctic Circle keeps an ice-free port thanks to the warm Gulf Stream, for all its Arctic position. Murmansk is the base of the icebreaker fleet and the chief sea gateway to the Russian Arctic.
fact: Moored permanently at a Murmansk quay is the Lenin, the world's first nuclear-powered icebreaker, now a museum.

name: Arkhangelsk
description: The city at the mouth of the Northern Dvina was Russia's first seaport and the country's main gateway to Europe before Saint Petersburg was founded. Arkhangelsk keeps close ties to shipbuilding and the timber industry of the Russian North.
fact: The city was founded in 1584 beside the Michael the Archangel monastery, from which it takes its name.

name: Veliky Novgorod
description: One of the oldest Russian cities was the centre of the medieval Novgorod Republic, with a popular assembly, the veche, a rare form of government in Rus. Its kremlin and the Millennium of Russia monument recall the city's place in the country's history.
fact: Hundreds of birch-bark letters have been found in Novgorod, everyday notes from the 11th to 15th centuries and a vital source on early Russian life.

name: Suzdal
description: This small town on the Golden Ring has kept dozens of churches, monasteries and wooden houses in an almost untouched historic setting, with no modern high-rise building at all. Suzdal remains one of the most visited destinations of old Rus.
fact: Tall buildings are banned in Suzdal, so the skyline is still set by the domes of its churches and bell towers.

name: Pskov
